articles.summary: Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE), a leading global markets operator and pioneer in equity and index derivatives, today announced the launch of mini-Russell 2000 Index (MRUT) binary options (ticker: MRTBW). The binary options based on MRUT, which is 1/10 th the size of the Russell 2000 Index, began trading on November 9 and are the latest addition to Cboe's prediction market suite. MRTBW are yes or no directional trades that pay $100 or $0, depending on whether the MRUT settles at, above or below the specified level. For example, an investor who makes a trade that MRUT will close above 280 will receive $100 at settlement if it closes at 280 or above, while the contract will pay $0 if the index closes below 280. Cboe will list P.M.-settled contracts expiring on the same and next trading day, and MRTBW options offerings are centrally cleared through the Options Clearing Corporation (OCC). articles.summary: Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE), a leading global markets operator and pioneer in equity and index derivatives, today issued the following statement in support of legal action filed by the Capital Markets Alliance (CMA) challenging the CFTC's approval of perpetual derivatives on U.S. stocks and ETFs. The CMA includes Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets Association: "Cboe has joined this action alongside some of the largest U.S. market participants and investor advocates because we believe the CFTC's actions threaten to erode the regulatory framework that has protected investors and governed U.S. securities markets for more than nine decades," said Craig Donohue, CEO of Cboe Global Markets. "Single-stock perpetual derivatives are the latest example of a troubling trend in which securities products are being offered on CFTC platforms – outside the appropriate regulatory framework and customer protection regime established by Congress.
